title: Transport Arrival in Exclusion Dynamics and Interacting Spin Chains: Exact Receiver Bounds and Coherent Pair Propagation
content: Transport in stochastic lattice gases and interacting quantum spin chains is commonlycharacterized by spreading profiles, conserved-density correlations and operator fronts. Thesediagnostics do not, by themselves, specify when a distant finite region can detect a localizedchange in preparation. We study this transport question through a receiver-dependentfirst-passage criterion: the earliest time at which measurements confined to that regiondistinguish two preparations above a prescribed threshold. Trace-distance discriminationsupplies the optimal benchmark, while restricted observable classes describe experimentallyspecified probes. For diagonal symmetric exclusion dynamics, one-particle duality gives anexact finite-block receiver likelihood. At half filling, its weighted occupation statistic yieldsa square-root dependence on receiver width; on the infinite lattice, the Bessel heat kerneldetermines a distance-dependent detection ceiling and two threshold crossings describedby distinct Lambert-W branches. An interacting charge-conserving spin model provides acomplementary exactly solvable regime: isolated excitations are stationary, whereas adjacentpairspropagatecoherentlywithaballisticfrontandanAiryturning-pointcorrection. Formoregeneral closed spin systems, we formulate the additional memory, mode-overlap and signal-separation conditions needed to relate receiver arrival to hydrodynamic transport. The anti-self-adjoint structure of the exact Mori fast block precludes a frequently assumed dissipativegap, and diffusion of charge alone does not constrain unrestricted local discrimination. XXZexact diagonalization and paired-preparation tensor-network calculations test the finite-sizediagnostics without asserting an unverified asymptotic exponent. Together, these resultsestablish receiver-dependent arrival laws in two solvable transport mechanisms and delimittheir extension to interacting many-body dynamics.
